overview: Black puts the knight on e4 where it can be harassed, usually after 3.Qe2 or 3.d3 Nc5 and then 4.d4 and Black's knight returns with tempo lost. White gets a free hand with space and development, while Black hopes to undermine the centre with ...d6 or ...f6 and use the dark squares. The opening is rare and mostly relies on surprise.

white_ideas.idea: 3.d3 or Qe2 to dislodge the knight and gain tempi
Build a big centre with d4 and Nf3 and take space

black_ideas.idea: ...Nc5 or ...Nxc3 and then ...d6 or ...f6 to break the centre
Play for counterplay on the dark squares against the e5 pawn

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e5 chain against ...d6 or ...f6 breaks and a pending ...c5

character.notes: Tricky and risky: Black is behind in development and needs counterplay; unbalanced rather than quiet.

gambit.notes: No material offered; tempo concession only.

soundness.notes: Considered inferior for Black; White gains time and space.

structure.notes: Advanced e5 pawn; the centre is not locked yet.

level.notes: Few forced lines but Black has to know how to handle an overextended centre.

character.reason: An unbalanced fight over e5 where Black must find counterplay.

soundness.reason: Black loses time for little and strong players avoid it.

structure.reason: The centre is not yet decided.

level.reason: Dubious so not beginner, few lines to learn.

plans.reason: White enjoys more space and tempo.
